---
title: "Measurement"
subtitle: "What is measured, what is not, and why a figure that exists can still not be a result."
---

## The short version

The harness decides what may be published, and right now it says "not this". Every evaluation
report in the repository is marked `quotable_as_a_result: false` with a reason, and the build will
not publish a figure from any of them.

That gate is the point of this page. A benchmark that only reports when the answer flatters you
is not a benchmark.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  REPORTS[(Eight evaluation reports)] --> CHECK{May it be quoted?}
  CHECK -->|No, all eight| REASON[Publish the reason]
  CHECK -->|Yes| NUMBER[Publish the number and its interval]
  REASON --> PAGE[Page]
  NUMBER --> PAGE
```

The right-hand path has not been taken yet. {{< var unmeasured_metrics >}} of
{{< var total_metrics >}} headline figures are waiting on the two inputs below.

## Three reasons a figure is not a result

The difference between them is the whole point.

### 1. Generated test data

A recording built from a specification rather than captured from a running system.

The headline finding of this project is that generated data is a **different difficulty**, not an
easier version of the same thing:

| Data | Root cause named correctly |
|---|---|
| Generated | Nearly all of them |
| Real recordings | {{< var recorded_root_cause_correct >}} of {{< var recorded_root_cause_applicable >}} |

The threshold tuned on generated data found a gap so wide it was implausible. The loudest quiet
system scored 7.7 and the quietest real incident scored 66.8, with no overlap at all. On real
recordings those two populations overlap badly.

A tuning run on generated data produced a number that looked excellent and generalised poorly.
This project exists to make that visible rather than to avoid it.

### 2. A partly recorded split

Eight of sixteen validation scenarios are recorded. A figure over those eight is a real
measurement of a small sample: true about the eight, silent about the split.

Reported with a bootstrap confidence interval rather than as a bare number, because an accuracy
over eight incidents and one over eighty are not the same kind of statement.

### 3. A split that was used for tuning

Thresholds and prompts were chosen using the validation split, so a figure from it measures
**fit**, not performance.

Only the two held-out splits can support a claim about performance, and both are empty.

::: {.callout-important}
## A stale report is worse than a missing one

One report here was computed over a single recording that was later deleted for corruption. It
describes a state that no longer exists, while still technically tracing to a report.

So the build compares each report's recorded count against the recordings actually present, and
refuses to publish from one that no longer matches. "Traceable" was not a strong enough property
on its own.
:::

## Two kinds of held-out test

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  LIB[114 scenario specs] --> TRAIN[train, 39]
  LIB --> VAL[validation, 16]
  LIB --> TID[test_id, 29]
  LIB --> TOOD[test_ood, 30]
  TRAIN --> TUNE[Used for tuning]
  VAL --> TUNE
  TID --> RESULT[The only figures that may be called a result]
  TOOD --> RESULT
```

They answer different questions:

- **test_id** holds back variants, load levels and seeds of fault types seen during development.
  It asks: *does it work?*
- **test_ood** holds back **entire fault families**. It asks: *did it generalise, or memorise?*

Splitting is by specification, not by recording, so a second recording of the same fault cannot
leak an answer across the boundary.

## The graders

| Grader | Asks |
|---|---|
| `root_cause` | Is the named service the injected one, at rank 1 |
| `root_cause_top3` | Is it anywhere in the top three |
| `abstention` | Did it stay quiet exactly when it should have |
| `fault_class` | Is the mechanism right, not just the service |
| `onset` | How far off is the stated start time |
| `evidence_validity` | Does every citation still return the same rows |
| `remediation` | Would the proposed fix have worked |

The first and third are a pair, and separating them matters. **One grader scoring both
identification and abstention would make a system that stays quiet about everything look like one
that identifies everything.** So a no-fault incident is *not applicable* to the root-cause
grader, and that is reported rather than counted as a pass.

## How a comparison is decided

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  CAND[Candidate] --> PAIR[Paired by incident]
  BASE[Baseline] --> PAIR
  PAIR --> BOOT[Paired bootstrap]
  BOOT --> ZERO{Interval excludes zero?}
  ZERO -->|No| NOTHING[Not a difference, nothing ships]
  ZERO -->|Yes| REAL[A measured difference]
```

Paired by incident rather than treated as two independent samples, so the interval reflects the
same incidents on both sides. **A difference whose interval includes zero is not a difference**,
and nothing ships on one.

The gate reports `INCONCLUSIVE` separately from `FAIL`, because "we measured a regression" and
"the sample is too small to rule one out" need different responses. The first is a bug. The
second is a recording session.

## The configurations compared

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `b0` | Statistics alone, no model. The floor every agent must beat |
| `b1` | A single-agent loop with the same tools |
| `b2` | The same loop without the knowledge graph |
| `fb-v1` | The full system |
| `a1` to `a6` | Ablations, each removing one component |

## Engineering, which is not performance

| | |
|---|---|
| Tests | {{< var tests_passed >}} passing, {{< var tests_skipped >}} skipped |
| Coverage | {{< var coverage_percent >}}%, against a floor of 85% |
| Decision records | {{< var adrs >}} |

::: {.callout-note}
A passing test says the code does what a test says it should. It says nothing about whether
Firebreak finds root causes. Keeping those two apart is most of what this page is for.
:::
